extracted.intended_audience: acute care hospital administrators, health system finance/compliance officers, hospital CFOs, Medicare policy stakeholders, health policy commenters
extracted.subtask_description: CMS proposed rule language describing the pricing, reconciliation, quality linkage, appeals, and overlap policies for the CJR-X episode-based payment model (LEJR episodes). This covers how target prices are constructed/adjusted, how annual reconciliation is performed, limits on participant risk, and rules for concurrent participation and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision and use of risk adjustment multipliers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use baseline data to calculate risk adjustment multipliers and hold them constant at reconciliation. Participants would be provided with these risk adjustment multipliers prior to the start of the performance year and would be able to use them to estimate their episode-level target prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multipliers would be calculated at the MS-DRG level (a separate set for each MS-DRG episode type). A prospective normalization factor would be incorporated into preliminary target prices and subject to a limited adjustment at reconciliation. CMS seeks comment on proposals at §§512.645(a-d) and §512.605 for the definitions of related risk adjustment factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reconciliation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct an annual reconciliation calculation comparing performance year spending on episodes with reconciliation target prices to determine reconciliation payments or repayments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One annual reconciliation per performance year is proposed to balance regular performance feedback with administrative burden. Reconcile all episodes attributed to a participant that end in a given fiscal year during the performance period (see §512.650).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation timing (claims runout and fiscal year alignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform reconciliation roughly 6 months after the end of the performance year to allow for claims runout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance years align with the federal fiscal year (October–September). CMS proposes to capture claims submitted by April 1 following the end of the performance year (6 months runout) and carry out the NPRA calculation. CMS cites internal data that ~98% of IP claims are received and ~90% considered final by 6 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy for participants experiencing reorganization events
rubrics_metrics.description: Define a 'reorganization event' (merger, consolidation, spin-off, other restructuring that results in a new hospital entity under a given CCN) and specify reconciliation treatment when billing CCNs change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform separate reconciliation calculations for the pre-effective-date episodes (anchor hospitalization admission or procedure before effective date) under the original CCN, and reconcile episodes on/after the effective date under the new/surviving CCN. If merged into or purchased by a non-CJR-X hospital that bills under a non-participant CCN, reconcile only episodes that occurred while the entity was a CJR-X participant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating preliminary target prices at reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: At reconciliation, apply beneficiary-level risk adjustment and limited adjustments to the prospective trend factor and normalization factor to preliminary target prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary target prices would also be adjusted for geographic wage factor updates to convert standardized dollars into unstandardized 'real' amounts. CMS proposes to update preliminary target prices to account for payment rule changes (e.g., CY OPPS/ASC and FY IPPS/LTCH PPS rules) during reconciliation target price construction (§512.645(g)). CMS considered but is not proposing to (a) update and deliver multiple preliminary target prices during the performance year or (b) remove the 3 percent cap on retrospective trend factor adjustments, citing participant predictability concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking Composite Quality Score (CQS) to discount factor and reconciliation eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate the Composite Quality Score into pricing by (1) requiring a minimum CQS for reconciliation payment eligibility and (2) determining the effective discount factor applied to reconciliation target prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 2.0 percent maximum discount factor is proposed in preliminary prices; high-quality performance can reduce that effective discount factor. The CQS categorization (Excellent/Good/Acceptable/Below Acceptable) determines discount reductions and payment eligibility. See specific category thresholds and effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality category thresholds and discount factor adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Define CQS ranges and associated payment/discount outcomes: 'Below Acceptable' (≤6.0), 'Acceptable' (6.1–12.0), 'Good' (12.1–17.0), and 'Excellent' (≥17.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants must achieve a minimum CQS ≥6.1 to be eligible for a reconciliation payment if actual episode spending is less than the reconciliation target price. 'Below Acceptable' (≤6.0) are ineligible for discount reductions and ineligible for reconciliation payments even if spending is below target. 'Acceptable' (6.1–12.0) are eligible for reconciliation payment but no discount reduction (2.0% applied). 'Good' (12.1–17.0) eligible and receive a 1.0% discount factor. 'Excellent' (≥17.1) eligible and receive a 0.0% discount factor. Stop-loss/stop-gain limits remain unchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of raw Net Payment Reconciliation Amount (NPRA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Retrospectively calculate a participant's performance year spending (with applicable caps/prorations) and compare aggregated performance year spending to aggregated reconciliation target prices to create the raw NPRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Episode spending subject to proration for services extending beyond the episode and capped at the high-cost outlier cap. Apply geographic wage factors to total capped episode spending to convert standardized dollars into 'real' amounts. Participants may have multiple target prices based on MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type and performance year when episode was initiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-cost outlier cap on episode spending
rubrics_metrics.description: Cap episode spending at the high-cost outlier cap to limit the effect of extreme-cost episodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 99th percentile for each MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type and region as the maximum; any episode spending above the cap is set to the amount of the high-cost outlier cap. Apply similarly to baseline and performance year episodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stop-loss and stop-gain limits on NPRA
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply symmetrical stop-loss and stop-gain limits as a percentage of a hospital's aggregate reconciliation target price to limit participant financial exposure and prevent excessive incentives to stint on care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose 20% stop-loss and stop-gain for most participants. Propose additional 5% stop-loss protection (not necessarily stop-gain) for certain categories: rural hospitals, Medicare-dependent small rural hospitals (MDH), sole community hospitals (SCH), and safety net hospitals (as defined at §512.605). The stop-loss limit does not apply to post-episode spending amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant responsibility for increased post-episode payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a post-episode spending policy to identify/mitigate inappropriate shifting of care outside the episode by calculating Medicare Parts A and B expenditures in the 30 days after episode completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify whether a participant's average 30-day post-episode spending in a performance year is greater than three standard deviations above the regional average (based on episodes in the same region). If above threshold, the participant would repay Medicare for the amount exceeding the threshold. Post-episode repayment is not subject to proposed stop-loss limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proration for services extending beyond the episode
rubrics_metrics.description: Prorate payments for services that extend beyond the episode when calculating episode spending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As described in §X.C.2.f.(3)(c), prorated treatment applies to services that extend past the episode boundary to appropriately attribute costs to the episode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of standardized dollars to unstandardized 'real' amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply geographic wage factors to total capped episode spending to convert standardized-dollar prices into unstandardized 'real' payment amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This conversion is applied both when converting preliminary/pre-reconciliation prices and when calculating performance-year spending for reconciliation comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation payment and repayment mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: If post-episode-adjusted NPRA is positive, participant receives a one-time lump sum reconciliation payment; if negative, participant owes a one-time lump sum repayment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS would collect repayments consistent with all relevant federal debt collection laws and regulations. This is consistent with the CJR Model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals process for reconciliation calculation errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow participants to submit a notice of calculation error regarding reconciliation reports if they believe an error occurred due to data quality, misapplication of methodology, or other issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participant must submit a timely error notice in writing within 30 calendar days of issuance of the performance report (CMS may specify form/manner/deadline). If no timely notice, reconciliation report deemed final and elements precluded from later contest. CMS would issue an initial determination in writing within 30 calendar days after receiving a timely notice (with possible extension). If participant disagrees, they or CMS may request reconsideration per the reconsideration review process at §512.190. Review limitations per §512.170 apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies on concurrent participation with other CMS models and initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Define when beneficiaries/providers can participate concurrently in CJR-X and other CMS models (e.g., total cost of care/ACO models) and when concurrent participation is not permitted (e.g., with TEAM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose allowing beneficiaries to be in a CJR-X episode and be attributed to a total cost of care/shared savings model; each participant retains savings for their model and reconciliation payments/repayments from one model are not included in the other's expenditures. Propose not to allow concurrent participation with TEAM: TEAM participants would be excluded from CJR-X (TEAM supersedes CJR-X for LEJR episodes at TEAM hospitals). If a TEAM episode overlaps a CJR-X episode (and vice versa), CMS proposes specific precedence rules so that the anchoring provider of the initial procedure remains accountable. The national set of LEJR episodes used for target price components will retain episodes even if not attributed to a participant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of national episode set for pricing
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain all national LEJR episodes in the national set used to calculate various CJR-X target price components, even if individual episodes are not attributed to CJR-X participants due to overlap with other models (e.g., TEAM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves the completeness of MS-DRG/HCPCS region combinations needed for constructing target price components across the model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capping retrospective trend factor adjustments (trend cap policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a 3 percent cap on retrospective trend factor adjustments applied at reconciliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS considered removing the 3% cap to fully account for realized performance-year spending and payment rule changes, but proposes to retain the cap to avoid target price instability and to help participants predict reconciliation target prices and assess spending performance.
